sections.overview: The Prowfish is a North Pacific marine fish, ranging from Japan and Russia through the Bering Sea to California.
sections.identification: It has a compressed body and rounded tail; reported adults may reach about 88 cm total length.
sections.habitat: Adults live near the bottom, with records from the surface to several hundred metres deep.
sections.diet: A study of the species found a diet dominated by gelatinous zooplankton, especially jellyfish and salps.
sections.behavior: Small juveniles shelter beneath jellyfish and may be mistaken for medusafishes.
sections.reproduction: The species accounts consulted provide little detail on its natural spawning or early development.
sections.ecology: It is an infrequent component of bottom-trawl survey catches in the northeast Pacific.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports no IUCN Red List assessment for this species.
